pages.ja:
彼にとって、その場所はあまりいい物ではなかった。
挫折と妄執、羨望と嫉妬。
昏い感情が染み付いたそこは、呪いの一室と言っていい。
本来自分の物である筈なのに、ただの一度も自分の為に使われなかった部屋。

pages.en:
To him, this was not a pleasant place.

Defeat and obsession. Longing and jealousy.

So thoroughly had those dark emotions soaked into the room that it might fairly be called accursed.

It should have belonged to him, yet not once had it ever been used for his sake.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The place is not too pleasant for him.
Frustration and delusion, envy and jealousy.
This place, permeated with emotions, is like a cursed room.
It should have been his, but this room was never used for him.

pages.ja:
「チ
陰気臭いんだよ、ここ」
舌打ちは、それこそ彼の妄想である。
どうでもいい余所の子供がここで数年を過ごし、長く間桐の血筋を脅かした。
彼が知り得る過去はそれだけだ。
父は何も語らなかったが、祖父はここで起きた事を一部始終教えてくれた。
父は自分を選ばず間桐家を絶やそうと考えたが、祖父は間桐家の再興を願っていた。

pages.en:
“Tch——this place is so damn gloomy.”

The contempt behind that click of his tongue rests upon fantasies of his own.

Some worthless, unrelated outsider's child spent several years here and long threatened the Matou bloodline.

That is all he can know of the past.

His father told him nothing, but his grandfather recounted everything that had taken place here.

His father refused to choose him and meant to let the Matou family die out. His grandfather wished to restore it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Damn
this place
stinks like piss.”
stinks.”
This is all his delusion.
A stranger’s child spent a few years in here and threatened the Matou blood for a long time.
That’s the only past he knows.
His father never said anything, but his grandfather told him a bit of what happened here.
His father did not choose him and decided to kill off the Matou blood, but his grandfather wished for the revival of the Matou family.

pages.ja:
だから、彼は父親だった人間になんの感情も抱いていない。
父は存在と落第を。
祖父は優越と権利を教えてくれた。
さて、そうなると母は何を与えてくれたのか、と考え、慎二は笑った。

pages.en:
And so he feels nothing for the man who was once his father.

His father taught him existence—and failure.

His grandfather taught him superiority and entitlement.

What, then, had his mother given him?

At the thought, Shinji laughs.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s why he has no feelings toward his father.
His father taught him existence and failure.
His grandfather taught him superiority and privilege.
Thinking about what his mother gave him, Shinji laughs.

pages.ja:
そもそも間桐の家に女などいらない。
母親はどこぞの保菌者だったと言うが、出産した後は用済みになったのだろう。
賭けてもいいが、この部屋を探せば母親だったモノぐらいある。
それを探す気など彼にはない。
そもそも、劣った自分を生んだ胎盤など見たくもない。

pages.en:
Women were never needed in the Matou family to begin with.

His mother had apparently been a carrier from some obscure bloodline. Once she gave birth, she must have outlived her usefulness.

He would wager that if he searched this room, he could find what remained of the woman who had been his mother.

He has no desire to look.

He has no wish to see the placenta that gave birth to an inferior creature like him.
pages.mirrorMoon:
First of all, women are not needed at the Matou household.
He heard that his mother is some Carrier, but she must have become useless after giving birth.
He can bet on it that he’ll find what used to be his mother in this room.
But he has no intention of searching for such a thing.
First of all, he does not want to see that which gave birth to his unskillful body.

地下室は腐敗に満ちている。
暗闇の奥、さらに暗い部分には、得体の知れない蟲どもが地面を覆っている。
もはや吸うべき養分などないだろうに、蟲は飽きずにこの地下修練場に巣くっている。

pages.en:
The cellar is steeped in decay.

Deep within the darkness, in places darker still, nameless vermin carpet the ground.

There should be nothing left here for them to feed upon, yet they continue to infest this underground training chamber without tiring.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The basement is filled with decay.
Strange worms are wriggling around deep within the dark.
There should not be any more nutrition to suck out of here, but the worms are still living here in this underground training area.

pages.ja:
……いや。
ここは元より人を育てる場所ではなく蟲を育てる場所。
這い寄る闇に見えるものは、黒い羽をもつ蟲の群れだ。
壁に張りついた影さえ、ヌメヌメと光る黒い粘虫に違いない。
その中に。
この最下層には不釣り合いな、黄金の輝きを放つ男がいた。

pages.en:
…No.

This was never a place for raising people. It was a place for raising worms.

What appears to be encroaching darkness is a swarm of black-winged insects.

Even the shadows clinging to the walls must be slick black grubs, gleaming wetly.

——And among them,

incongruous in this lowest depth, stands a man radiant with gold.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…No.
From the beginning, this place has been used not to raise people, but to raise bugs.
What can be seen inside the dark are swarms of bugs with black wings.
Even the shadows on the walls must be black bugs.
In it all…
A golden man unsuited to this lowest pit is there.

Those red eyes turn casually toward him.

The red eyes cow him, but Shinji continues to approach.

Uncanny as Archer may be, to him the creature is only a familiar—his Servant—and nothing more.

And so he maintains his arrogance before Archer at all times.

His words are generous, each one calculated to demonstrate that he remains the one with power.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Shinji’s pressured by the red eyes, but he still approaches Archer.
Even if Archer may be an ominous existence, he is only a Servant.
Therefore, he maintains his arrogance against Archer.
He shows leniency, but he still displays that he is the stronger one.

pages.en:
“——I see. Kotomine appears to value you quite highly.”

“Yeah. He said he owes Grandfather. Something about how an old bloodline like mine deserves to win instead of some dubious third-rate mage.

“——Hah. That's obvious, isn't it? Hardly worth saying, but at least he knows quality when he sees it. He's been helpful, too, so I'm considering giving him some reward once I have the Holy Grail.”

His delighted snicker echoes through the cellar.
pages.mirrorMoon:

I see. Kotomine thinks highly of you, huh?”

Hah, that’s obvious. He’s stating the obvious, but he’s good at determining who’s strong. I’m thinking about maybe thanking him if I obtain the Holy Grail.”
Joyful laughter echoes through the room.

“——Then let's get started, Archer. We don't need to worry about being seen anymore. Go slaughter people by the score, devour all the souls you can, and make yourself stronger.

“…After that, they're next. We'll crush that eyesore Saber and pay Emiya back for everything he did.”

“Come on,” he says, reaching for Archer's shoulder.

Archer studies the hand as though it has touched something foul.

He pats Archer on the shoulder.
Archer watches as if something unpleasant has touched him.

“What? Come on, Archer, I said we're leaving.

“I don't care what kind of hero you used to be. Servants have to obey their Masters absolutely, don't they?”

Perhaps he imagines Saber brought to heel and his friend made to grovel before him.

Still in high spirits, he issues his command to Archer.

But the golden youth does not move so much as a hair.

“——Shinji. You do not understand the Holy Grail.”

For the first time, he speaks his Master's name.

“If you desire the Holy Grail, leave the other Masters alone. They are sacrifices, nothing more. If you truly mean to take the Grail, there is something else that must first be secured.”

“Something we have to secure first…?”

One foot has withdrawn without his noticing, and the hand on Archer's shoulder has somehow fallen away.

A Heroic Spirit who should not exist.

The mightiest King of Heroes, said to have remained in this world since the previous Holy Grail War——

pages.en:
“What is it? Ask, and I shall answer, Master.”

“Your wish. Once you get the Holy Grail, what do you plan to do with it, Archer?”

It is, in its way, the most natural question imaginable.

A Heroic Spirit who has come halfway to ageless immortality and possesses every treasure in the world.

What can such a man still desire?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What? I shall answer you if you question me, Master.”
“It’s about your wish. What do you want to do after you obtain the Holy Grail, Archer?”
It’s a natural question.
A heroic spirit that is half immortal and has all the treasures in the world.
What can this man possibly wish for now?

なんだ。そんな事も知らなかったのか」

“——What? You did not even know that?”

Archer sounds genuinely surprised.

His face opens into a smile, as though he has stumbled upon some small happiness.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
What? You did not know?”
Archer says so with surprise.
His face is smiling as if he found a small happiness.

余分なモノに与える意義などない」
「……余分な、モノ……？」
「昔の話なのだがな。十人の奴隷を選び、その中で“いなくともよい”モノを殺そうとした事がある。どうなったと思う、シンジ？」

pages.en:
“I permit luxury. Ornate splendor is worthy of the highest admiration. But——there is no value in granting anything to what is *superfluous*.”

“…What is… superfluous?”

“This is a tale from long ago. I once chose ten slaves and resolved to kill whichever of them was unnecessary. What do you suppose happened, Shinji?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I allow everything that is magnificent. A splendid ornament is something I must admire the most. But
I cannot stand giving it to the meaningless extras.”
“…Extras…?”
“It happened a long time ago. I chose ten servants and tried to kill the one that I did not need. What do you think happened, Shinji?”

pages.ja:
「はあ？ みんな奴隷なんだろ。なら全員殺したんじゃないの」
「いやいや。それがな、一人も殺せなかった。いかな人足とは言え無駄なモノなどいなかったのだ、かつての世界には」
皮肉げに肩をすくめ、アーチャーは一歩前に出た。
……いっそう深い闇。
暗い影に覆われた床に向けて足を上げる。
pages.jaRuby:

皮肉げに肩をすくめ、アーチャーは一歩前に出た。
……いっそう深い闇。
暗い影に覆われた床に向けて足を上げる。
pages.en:
“What? They were all slaves, weren't they? So you killed every one of them.”

“No, no. In the end, I could not kill a single one. However lowly a laborer might be, no one in the world of old was without purpose.”

Archer shrugs with sardonic amusement and steps forward.

…Into a deeper darkness.

He raises one foot above the floor swallowed in black shadow.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh? They were all slaves, right? Then didn’t you kill them all?”
“No. I actually could not kill anybody. None of the laborers were meaningless in the old world.”
He shrugs his shoulders ironically and steps forward.
…A deeper darkness.
He raises his foot over the dark shadow.

pages.ja:
「だがこの世界には余分が溢れている。十人どころか千人という人間を選んだところで、殺せない人間など出てきまい。
まったく、おそろしく人間に優しい世界になったものだ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“But this world overflows with excess. Choose not ten people but a thousand, and I doubt you would find a single one who could not be killed.

“——Truly, the world has become remarkably kind to mankind.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But this world is filled with extras. I believe there would not be a single meaningful person even if I sought through a thousand people.
Man, this world has gotten so friendly to humans.”

pages.jaRuby: 「簡単な話だ。多いという事は、それだけで気色が悪い」
pages.en: “It is quite simple. Mere abundance is repulsive.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “It is a simple thing. A lot of something is ugly by itself.”

pages.jaRuby: 上げた片足を、深い闇へと踏み下ろした。

pages.mirrorMoon: …Lowers his raised foot into the darkness.

踏みしだかれた暗い床には夥しい蟲の死骸と、更に夥しく集る、有象無象の群があった。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…A wet crunch.

The dark floor beneath his heel is littered with the corpses of countless worms—and a still greater horde of nameless things swarming over them.

…A smashing sound.
On the ground are numerous smashed bugs, with more swarming around.
